title: Bennie Moten as the greatest bandleader
summary: Jones calls Bennie Moten the greatest bandleader of all, the source of later styles, who came to New York first in 1930 with Jimmy Rushing.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Bennie Moten was a great pianist, wasn't he?

Bennie Moten was the greatest bandleader that ever lived. Whenever you saw piano; whenever you saw a Fletcher Henderson; whenever you saw a Cab Calloway; whenever you saw a Duke Ellington... - that's Bennie Moten. You see Basie, that's Bennie Moten. The greatest bandleader; he covered the whole sphere. Everybody thought Jimmy Rushing was Bennie Moten when they came to New York in 1930 and 1932, but he was Mr. Moten.
Bennie Moten! But you never saw Bennie.
Was Jimmy Rushing with Bennie Moten when he came here in 1930?
I see. Who else was in that band?
